title: Classic Brown Sugar Banana Bread
description: A moist, tender loaf with deep banana flavor from very ripe fruit, brown sugar, and a spoonful of yogurt. One bowl for the wet ingredients, one for the dry, and no mixer.
notes: Use bananas that are heavily speckled or fully brown; yellow bananas make a bland, pale loaf. Measure the mashed banana, since too much makes the center gummy. Cool at least 1 hour before slicing so the crumb sets. Keeps wrapped at room temperature for 3 days, or freeze slices for up to 3 months. Sour cream can replace the yogurt. To add walnuts or chocolate chips, fold in 3/4 cup with the flour (this changes the allergens).

ingredients.name: mashed very ripe bananas (3 large or 4 medium, 340 g)
unsalted butter, melted and cooled (113 g)
turbinado or granulated sugar, for the top

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan and line it with a strip of parchment that overhangs the two long sides so you can lift the loaf out.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon until evenly combined.

In a large bowl, mash the bananas with a fork until mostly smooth with a few small lumps, and check that you have 1 1/2 cups. Whisk in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs, yogurt, and vanilla until the mixture looks uniform.
Add the flour mixture and fold with a spatula just until no dry flour remains. The batter should be thick and a little lumpy; stop mixing as soon as it comes together so the loaf stays tender.
Scrape the batter into the prepared pan, smooth the top, and sprinkle with the turbinado sugar if using.

Bake until the loaf is deep golden brown and a toothpick pushed into the center comes out with a few moist crumbs and no wet batter, 55 to 65 minutes (200 to 205°F inside). If the top is browning quickly after 40 minutes, lay a piece of foil loosely over it.
Cool in the pan on a wire rack for 15 minutes, then lift the loaf out by the parchment and cool for at least 1 hour before slicing.

title: Fudgy Almond Flour Brownies
description: Dense, chewy brownies with a shiny, crackled top, made with almond flour and melted dark chocolate instead of wheat flour. They happen to be gluten-free, and nobody will ask.
notes: Contains almonds (tree nuts). Most bittersweet chocolate contains soy lecithin and may contain milk; check the label, and choose chocolate and cocoa labeled gluten-free if baking for someone with celiac disease. Use blanched, finely ground almond flour, not coarse almond meal. These are fragile while warm, so cool completely (about 1 1/2 hours) before cutting; 30 minutes in the refrigerator gives the cleanest squares. Store airtight at room temperature for 4 days or freeze for 3 months. A glass pan needs about 5 extra minutes.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, cut into pieces (113 g)
flaky sea salt, for the top

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Line an 8x8-inch metal baking pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides, and lightly grease the parchment.

Put the butter and chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water (or microwave in 30-second bursts) and stir until melted and smooth, 3 to 4 minutes. Take the bowl off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes so it is warm, not hot.

Whisk in the granulated sugar and brown sugar. Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, and whisk hard for 1 full minute until the batter turns glossy, thickens, and pulls away from the side of the bowl. This is what gives the shiny, crackled top.
Sift the cocoa powder over the batter, add the almond flour and fine salt, and fold with a spatula until no dry pockets remain.

Spread the batter evenly in the prepared pan and sprinkle with flaky salt if using. Bake until the top is shiny and set, the edges are slightly puffed, and a toothpick inserted 1 inch from the edge comes out with moist crumbs, 25 to 30 minutes. The center should look just set, not liquid.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, at least 1 1/2 hours. Lift out by the parchment and cut into 16 squares, wiping the knife between cuts.

title: One-Bowl Vegan Chocolate Cake
description: A soft, dark chocolate snack cake that gets its lift from baking soda and vinegar rather than eggs, finished with a glossy cocoa glaze. It mixes in one bowl with a whisk in about ten minutes.
notes: Use natural (not Dutch-process) cocoa in the cake if you can; either works in the glaze. Brewed coffee deepens the chocolate flavor without tasting like coffee. Get the batter into the oven soon after mixing, because the baking soda starts working as soon as the vinegar goes in. Glaze only when the cake is fully cool, about 1 hour. Keeps covered at room temperature for 3 days. Some cane sugar is filtered with bone char; choose organic or beet sugar if that matters to you. The batter also makes 12 cupcakes, baked 18 to 22 minutes.

ingredients.name: warm water or brewed coffee (240 ml)
neutral oil, such as canola or sunflower
white vinegar or apple cider vinegar
hot water or hot coffee, plus more as needed

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Grease an 8x8-inch baking pan with oil and line the bottom with parchment.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour, granulated sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt until no lumps of cocoa remain.
Add the warm water or coffee, oil, vinegar, and vanilla. Whisk just until the batter is smooth, about 30 seconds. It will be thin and pourable.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan right away. Bake until the top springs back when pressed lightly and a toothpick in the center comes out clean or with a few dry crumbs, 30 to 35 minutes.
Cool the cake completely in the pan on a wire rack, about 1 hour.

For the glaze, whisk the powdered sugar, cocoa powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Add the hot water and oil and whisk until smooth, glossy, and thick but pourable, adding more hot water 1 teaspoon at a time if it is too stiff to spread.
Spread the glaze over the cooled cake and let it set for 20 minutes before cutting into 9 squares.

title: Mixed Berry Oat Crisp
description: Juicy berries baked under a buttery brown sugar and oat topping that stays crunchy. It works with fresh or frozen fruit, so you can make it any time of year.
notes: Any mix of blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, and hulled strawberries works; cut large strawberries into quarters. With frozen berries, do not thaw them, use 3 tablespoons cornstarch instead of 2, and bake 50 to 55 minutes. The filling must bubble in the center, not just at the edges, or the cornstarch will not thicken. Let it rest 20 minutes before serving so the juices set. Leftovers keep covered in the refrigerator for 4 days; rewarm at 350°F for 10 to 15 minutes to crisp the topping again. The topping can be made 2 days ahead and kept chilled.

ingredients.name: mixed berries, fresh or frozen (about 800 g)
cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes (85 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center. Set an 8x8-inch or 2-quart baking dish on a rimmed baking sheet to catch any drips.

For the filling, put the berries in the baking dish and add the granulated sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, vanilla, and pinch of salt. Toss gently until the berries are coated and no white streaks of cornstarch remain, then spread in an even layer.

For the topping, whisk the flour, oats, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt in a medium bowl. Add the cold butter and rub it in with your fingertips until no dry flour remains and the mixture forms clumps ranging from pea-sized to marble-sized, 2 to 3 minutes.
Scatter the topping evenly over the berries, leaving the clumps intact rather than pressing them down.

Bake until the topping is deep golden brown and the juices are bubbling thickly in the center of the dish, 40 to 45 minutes. If the topping browns before the center bubbles, cover loosely with foil and keep baking.
Let the crisp rest for 20 minutes so the juices thicken, then serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Classic Caramel Flan
description: A silky baked custard of eggs and milk that turns out of the pan under its own amber caramel sauce. It needs only a handful of pantry ingredients and is best made the day before.
equipment: roasting pan for a water bath
notes: Use a solid cake pan, not a springform, which will leak. The flan must chill at least 6 hours, and overnight is better, so the custard firms up and the hardened caramel dissolves into a sauce. The gentle water bath keeps the eggs from curdling; pull the flan when the center still jiggles like gelatin (170 to 175°F), because it finishes setting as it cools. Bubbles or a spongy texture mean it was overbaked or the water was boiling. Hot caramel causes serious burns, so do not touch or taste it. Keeps covered in the refrigerator for 4 days.
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center and bring a kettle of water to a boil. Set an 8-inch round cake pan inside a roasting pan.

For the caramel, combine the sugar and water in a small heavy saucepan over medium heat and stir only until the sugar dissolves. Then cook without stirring, swirling the pan now and then, until the syrup turns deep amber, 8 to 10 minutes. Immediately pour it into the cake pan and tilt the pan to coat the bottom. It will harden as it cools.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs gently until blended, trying not to whip in foam. Whisk in the condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla, and salt until smooth.
Pour the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into the caramel-lined pan. Cover the pan loosely with foil.
Set the roasting pan on the oven rack and carefully pour hot water from the kettle into it until the water comes halfway up the side of the cake pan.
Bake until the edges are set and the center 2 inches still jiggles like gelatin when you nudge the pan, 45 to 55 minutes (170 to 175°F in the center).
Lift the cake pan out of the water and cool on a wire rack for 1 hour. Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
To serve, run a thin knife around the edge of the flan. Place a rimmed serving plate upside down over the pan, flip both together, and lift the pan away, letting the caramel sauce run over the top.

title: No-Knead Rosemary Focaccia
description: A tall, airy focaccia with a crisp olive oil crust and an open, chewy crumb. The dough is stirred together in one bowl and time does the kneading for you.
notes: Plan on 2 1/2 to 3 hours of rising time in addition to the hands-on and baking time. Water for the dough should feel warm, not hot (100 to 110°F); hotter water can kill the yeast. Go by how the dough looks rather than the clock: in a cool kitchen the rises take longer. For more flavor, let the first rise happen in the refrigerator for 12 to 18 hours, then continue with the pan rise, which will take 1 1/2 to 2 hours from cold. Active dry yeast works in the same amount; stir it into the warm water first and wait 5 minutes. If your pan tends to stick, line it with parchment before oiling. Best the day it is baked; rewarm leftovers at 375°F for 5 to 8 minutes, or freeze for up to 1 month.

ingredients.name: bread flour or all-purpose flour (500 g)

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, yeast, fine salt, and sugar. Add the warm water (100 to 110°F) and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and stir with a spatula until no dry flour remains, about 1 minute. The dough will be wet, sticky, and shaggy.

Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm spot until doubled in size and bubbly on the surface, 1 1/2 to 2 hours. About 30 minutes in, wet your hand and fold the edges of the dough up and over the center 4 times, turning the bowl as you go, to build some strength.

Pour 2 tablespoons of the olive oil into a 9x13-inch metal baking pan and coat the bottom and sides. Scrape the dough into the pan, turn it once to coat with oil, and gently stretch it toward the corners. If it springs back, let it rest 10 minutes and stretch again.
Let the dough rise uncovered until puffy, nearly doubled, and jiggly when you shake the pan, 45 to 60 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the center.

Drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil over the dough. Oil your fingers and press them straight down to the bottom of the pan all over to make deep dimples. Scatter the rosemary leaves and flaky salt over the top.
Bake until the top and edges are deep golden brown and the bottom is crisp, 22 to 26 minutes (205 to 210°F in the center).
Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then slide the focaccia onto a wire rack so the bottom stays crisp. Let it cool at least 15 minutes before cutting into 12 pieces.

title: Soft Cinnamon Sugar Snickerdoodles
description: Thick, soft cookies with crinkled tops, a cinnamon sugar crust, and the gentle tang that cream of tartar gives a true snickerdoodle. No chilling needed.
notes: Allergens: contains milk (butter), eggs, and wheat. There are no nuts or peanuts in the recipe. Cream of tartar gives the classic tang and chew, so do not skip it; if you must, replace both the cream of tartar and baking soda with 2 teaspoons baking powder for a milder cookie. Pull the cookies while the centers still look slightly underdone; they firm up on the hot sheet. Cook time covers three sheets baked one at a time. Store airtight at room temperature for 5 days. Rolled and coated dough balls freeze for 2 months; bake from frozen, adding 1 to 2 minutes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center. Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment. In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt.

In a large bowl, beat the softened butter and 1 1/2 cups sugar with a mixer on medium-high speed until pale and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, scraping down the bowl.
Add the flour mixture and mix on low speed just until no streaks of flour remain. The dough should be soft but not sticky; if it is too soft to roll, refrigerate it for 20 minutes.
Stir the 1/4 cup sugar and the cinnamon together in a shallow bowl. Scoop the dough into 1 1/2-tablespoon portions, roll each into a ball, and roll in the cinnamon sugar to coat generously.
Arrange the balls 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets, about 12 per sheet. Do not flatten them.
Bake one sheet at a time until the cookies are puffed, the tops are cracked, and the edges are set while the centers still look soft and slightly underdone, 9 to 11 minutes.
Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, where they will settle and crinkle, then move them to a wire rack to cool completely. Repeat with the remaining dough on a cooled sheet.

title: Extra-Smooth Lemon Tahini Hummus
description: Light, creamy hummus made from canned chickpeas simmered until they fall apart, then blended warm with plenty of tahini, lemon, and ice water. The short simmer is what makes it smooth without peeling a single chickpea.
notes: Contains sesame (tahini). Makes about 3 cups. Use a pourable, well-stirred tahini; a bitter or stiff one will carry through to the hummus. Stop adding ice water when the hummus is a little looser than you want, because it firms up as it cools. Keeps in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 5 days; let it sit at room temperature for 20 minutes and stir in a splash of water before serving. Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers to keep it gluten-free; pita adds wheat.

ingredients.name: chickpeas (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
fresh lemon juice (from 1 to 2 lemons), plus more to taste
fine sea salt, plus more to taste
ice water, plus more as needed

instructions: Put the chickpeas and baking soda in a medium saucepan and cover with water by 2 inches. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat and simmer until the chickpeas are very soft and falling apart, with skins floating loose, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain in a colander and rinse briefly with hot water.
While the chickpeas simmer, combine the lemon juice, garlic, and salt in a food processor and pulse a few times. Let it sit for 10 minutes; the lemon takes the raw edge off the garlic.
Add the tahini and process for 1 minute until thick and pale. With the motor running, pour in the 4 tablespoons ice water and process until the mixture is smooth and fluffy.

Add the warm chickpeas and the cumin. Process for 3 to 4 minutes, stopping to scrape down the bowl, until completely smooth. Add more ice water 1 tablespoon at a time until the hummus is creamy and slightly looser than you want it.
Taste and adjust with more salt or lemon juice until it tastes bright and well seasoned.
Spread the hummus in a shallow bowl, make a swirl with the back of a spoon, and top with the olive oil, paprika or sumac, and parsley if using. Serve at room temperature.

title: Baked Vegetable Spring Rolls
description: Crisp, blistered spring rolls filled with gingery cabbage, carrot, and shiitake mushrooms, baked on a sheet pan instead of deep-fried. A good make-ahead appetizer for a crowd.
notes: Buy thin wheat spring roll pastry (usually sold frozen), not rice paper and not thicker egg roll wrappers, which contain egg. Check the label to confirm the wrappers are egg-free if you need the rolls to be vegan. The filling must be cooled and well drained before wrapping, or the rolls will steam and turn soggy. Brushing every surface with oil is what makes them crisp and golden. To make ahead, freeze the unbaked rolls on a tray, then bag them for up to 2 months; brush with oil and bake from frozen at 425°F for 25 to 28 minutes. Check the sweet chili sauce label for allergens if serving it.

ingredients.name: cornstarch, stirred into 2 tablespoons cold water, for sealing
shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and thinly sliced
medium carrots, peeled and coarsely grated
wheat spring roll pastry wrappers (8-inch square, egg-free), thawed

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Stir the cornstarch and cold water together in a small bowl and set it near your work surface.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook until browned, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the cabbage, carrots, and salt and stir-fry until the vegetables are wilted and the pan is nearly dry, 4 to 5 minutes.

Take the pan off the heat and stir in the scallions, soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper. Spread the filling on a large plate and let it cool for 15 minutes, then pour off any liquid that collects.

Place one wrapper on the counter with a corner pointing toward you, keeping the rest covered with a damp towel. Spoon 2 to 3 tablespoons of filling in a short log across the lower third. Fold the bottom corner up over the filling and tuck it in snugly, fold in the two sides, and roll up tightly. Stir the cornstarch mixture, dab it on the top corner, and press to seal.
Set the roll seam side down on the baking sheet and repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling, spacing the rolls 1 inch apart. Brush each roll all over with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil.
Bake for 20 to 24 minutes, turning the rolls over halfway through, until golden brown, blistered, and crisp on all sides.
Let the rolls cool for 5 minutes, since the filling is very hot, then serve with sweet chili sauce for dipping.

title: No-Bake Sunflower Seed Energy Bites
description: Chewy oat bites held together with sunflower seed butter and maple syrup, packed with flax, chia, and pumpkin seeds. They are free of nuts and peanuts, so they are easy to pack for school or the office.
notes: Use oats labeled certified gluten-free; regular oats are often cross-contaminated with wheat. When making these for someone with a nut allergy, check that the seed butter, seeds, and dried fruit are packed in a nut-free facility. The mixture needs 30 minutes in the refrigerator before rolling. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 1 week or freeze for 3 months. For a chocolate version, swap the dried fruit for 1/3 cup dairy-free mini chocolate chips (check the label for soy and milk). If nuts are not a concern, peanut or almond butter can replace the sunflower seed butter, which adds peanuts or tree nuts.

ingredients.name: certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (113 g)
sunflower seed butter, well stirred (130 g)
raisins or dried cranberries, roughly chopped

instructions: In a large bowl, stir together the oats, ground flaxseed, pumpkin seeds, chia seeds, cinnamon, and salt.
In a small bowl, stir the sunflower seed butter, maple syrup, and vanilla until smooth. If the seed butter is stiff, warm it in the microwave for 15 to 20 seconds first so it loosens.

Pour the seed butter mixture over the oat mixture, add the dried fruit, and stir and press with a spatula until everything is evenly coated and no dry oats remain, 1 to 2 minutes. A handful should hold together when squeezed; if it crumbles, add 1 more tablespoon maple syrup, and if it is too sticky, add 1 to 2 tablespoons oats.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate until the mixture is firm enough to roll, about 30 minutes.
Scoop the mixture into 1 1/2-tablespoon portions and roll firmly between slightly damp palms to make 18 balls.
Arrange the bites in an airtight container and chill for 15 minutes more to set before eating.
